title: Personal agent pattern
lede: One person, one agent. The Ping Agentic Control Plane decides at three points: who the user is (Agent IAM Core), which tools the agent may use (Agent Privilege, which is also the MCP front door) and what the business rules allow (Agent Authorize). Everything here is simulated.

steps.title: The user asks
steps.what: The user asks their own agent for something. The agent acts for one person.

steps.title: The agent plans
steps.what: The agent uses a language model to choose a tool. The model never holds a credential.

steps.title: The user authenticates
steps.what: Agent IAM Core signs the user in. The token is for Agent Privilege: aud https://aigateway.example, sub user.

steps.title: Agent Privilege checks the tool
steps.what: The agent calls Agent Privilege over MCP with that token. Agent Privilege applies tool-level (coarse to medium grained) authorization: may this user, through this agent, call this tool at all?

steps.title: Token exchange (OBO, coming soon)
steps.what: Not available yet. When it is, Agent Privilege will swap the token for an on-behalf-of token for the MCP server (aud https://mcpserver.example, same sub), and it depends on MCP support. Until then the next call uses the credential the MCP server accepts.

steps.title: Agent Privilege calls the MCP server
steps.what: Agent Privilege uses the credential that server needs: OIDC, a static token or an API key.

steps.title: The MCP server calls the API
steps.what: The MCP server reaches the backend through the API gateway.

steps.title: Fine grained authorization
steps.what: Agent Authorize applies finer-grained, business-level rules to this request and data.

steps.title: The resource
steps.what: Only a request that passed both layers reaches the resource.
